exercises.label: Exercise 14.B1 — Medium: Carry a bounded sensor bias through feedback
exercises.thoroughness_rationale: The current expanded answer has the correct four results, but the ultimate bound skips the first recurrence substitutions and finite geometric-sum denominator, and checks the actuator only after declaring invariance. Derive the bias disturbance decomposition, verify actuator applicability on the same region, prove the induction, then unroll the inequality and translate its limit into temperature units.
exercises.replacement_html:
Separate the nominal feedback map from the sensor error. With bias $b_t$ and disturbance $w_t$, the actual update is $e_{t+1}=0.9e_t-0.3\tanh(e_t+b_t)+w_t$. Define $F(e)=0.9e-0.3\tanh(e)$. Since $F(0)=0$ and

$$F'(e)=0.9-0.3(1-\tanh^2e),\qquad0.6\le F'(e)\le0.9,$$

the mean-value theorem gives $|F(e)|\le0.9|e|$. The derivative of tanh has magnitude at most1, so the same theorem gives $|\tanh(e+b)-\tanh(e)|\le|b|$.

Insert and subtract the nominal tanh term:

$$e_{t+1}=F(e_t)-0.3\bigl(\tanh(e_t+b_t)-\tanh(e_t)\bigr)+w_t.$$

Using $|b_t|\le0.03$ and $|w_t|\le0.02$ with the triangle inequality therefore yields

$$|e_{t+1}|\le0.9|e_t|+0.3(0.03)+0.02 =0.9|e_t|+0.009+0.02 =0.9|e_t|+0.029.$$

Check that the stated controller can actually be applied in the operating region. If $|e_t|\le0.5$, the measured error satisfies $|e_t+b_t|\le0.5+0.03=0.53$. Tanh is odd and increasing, so

$$|u_t|=1.5|\tanh(e_t+b_t)| \le1.5\tanh(0.53)\approx0.728072\ \text{kilowatts}\lt0.8\ \text{kilowatts}.$$

The actuator does not clip the requested command on this region. Thus the assumed closed-loop equation remains applicable there.

Prove containment one update at a time. At any allowed current state, $|e_{t+1}|\le0.9(0.5)+0.029=0.45+0.029=0.479\le0.5$. Starting with $|e_0|\le0.5$, the same argument applies at every later step: the state remains in the locally modeled region and the actuator remains within its limit. This induction covers every sequence of biases and disturbances satisfying the bounds, without assuming a favorable sign or independence.

Unroll the recurrence to obtain the ultimate error bound. Let $r_t=|e_t|$. The first two substitutions are $r_1\le0.9r_0+0.029$ and $r_2\le0.9^2r_0+0.029(0.9+1)$. Continuing by induction gives

$$\begin{aligned} r_t&\le0.9^t r_0+0.029\sum_{j=0}^{t-1}0.9^j\\ &=0.9^t r_0+0.029\frac{1-0.9^t}{1-0.9}\\ &=0.9^t r_0+0.29(1-0.9^t). \end{aligned}$$

The finite geometric sum comes from multiplying the sum by0.9 and subtracting; the denominator is $1-0.9=0.1$. Since $0.9^t\to0$, this proves $\limsup_{t\to\infty}|e_t|\le0.29$. The normalization $T_t-40=10e_t$ converts that to $\limsup_t|T_t-40|\le2.9$ degrees Celsius.

This is a sufficient ultimate bound, not a claim that every trajectory converges to the reference or enters the exact ultimate interval in finite time. Persistent bias and disturbance may prevent zero error. The certificate concerns the stated minute-sampled, no-delay model and its valid region; it does not supply an intersample temperature guarantee.

exercises.label: Exercise 14.B2 — Hard: A stable delayed loop can leave the temperature box
exercises.thoroughness_rationale: The delayed-state answer derives the augmented matrix determinant and discriminant, gives both complex roots and their squared magnitude, and states the linear discrete-time stability implication. It separately evaluates an explicitly allowed independently initialized memory pair, checks its0.6 successor and0.75-kilowatt initial actuator command, and respects the question’s no-prehistory qualifier. Thus convergence is not confused with square containment and each requested calculation is visible.
exercises.replacement_html:
1. Include controller memory in the state. With $z_t=(e_t,e_{t-1})^\top$, the delayed linear loop is $z_{t+1}=A_dz_t$, where $A_d=\begin{bmatrix}0.9&-0.3\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$. Its characteristic polynomial is $\det(\lambda I-A_d)=\lambda(\lambda-0.9)+0.3=\lambda^2-0.9\lambda+0.3$.

2. Check asymptotic stability. The discriminant is $0.9^2-4(0.3)=0.81-1.2=-0.39$. Thus the roots are $0.45\pm i\sqrt{39}/20\approx0.45\pm0.312250i$. Their squared magnitude is $0.45^2+39/400=0.2025+0.0975=0.3$, so both have magnitude $\sqrt{0.3}\approx0.547723\lt1$. A finite linear discrete-time system with all eigenvalues strictly inside the unit circle has $A_d^t\to0$, hence every augmented trajectory converges to zero.

3. Test containment independently of convergence. The initialization model permits $z_0=(0.5,-0.5)$ in the square. Its next current error is $e_1=0.9(0.5)-0.3(-0.5)=0.45+0.15=0.6\gt0.5$, so the square is not invariant. The initial command is $u_0=-1.5(-0.5)=0.75$ kilowatts, within the $0.8$ limit; saturation is not responsible.

No actuator-bounded prehistory needs to produce this initialized memory pair under the question's assumptions. Stability guarantees eventual convergence, while invariance requires every next state to remain in the permitted set. A delay-aware safety design needs an invariant region in both coordinates whose projection respects the physical temperature limit.

exercises.label: Easy 1 — Find the equilibrium before shifting
exercises.thoroughness_rationale: The current result is right but compresses controller substitution, equilibrium rearrangement and cancellation into short assertions. Show the full affine closed loop, solve and verify both equilibrium coordinates, expand the shifted dynamics, and test the unshifted origin directly.
exercises.replacement_html:
First substitute the controller into the plant. The update is $x_{t+1}=0.5x_t+u_t$, and the controller uses $u_t=0.25x_t+1$. Therefore

$$x_{t+1}=0.5x_t+(0.25x_t+1) =(0.5+0.25)x_t+1=0.75x_t+1.$$

Solve for the constant state and its corresponding command. An equilibrium has $x_{t+1}=x_t=x_*$, so

$$x_*=0.75x_*+1 \iff(1-0.75)x_*=1 \iff0.25x_*=1 \iff x_*=4.$$

The equilibrium command is $u_*=0.25(4)+1=1+1=2$. Checking the original plant gives $0.5x_*+u_*=0.5(4)+2=4=x_*$, so both coordinates are consistent.

Measure deviations from that equilibrium. Define $\tilde x_t=x_t-4$. Then $x_t=\tilde x_t+4$, and

$$\begin{aligned} \tilde x_{t+1}&=x_{t+1}-4 =0.75(\tilde x_t+4)+1-4\\ &=0.75\tilde x_t+3+1-4 =0.75\tilde x_t. \end{aligned}$$

The input deviation is likewise $u_t-2=0.25(x_t-4)=0.25\tilde x_t$. Repeated substitution gives $\tilde x_t=0.75^t\tilde x_0$, which tends to zero because $|0.75|\lt1$.

Check the original origin rather than confusing it with the shifted one. At $x_t=0$, the controller gives $u_t=1$ and the next state is $0.5(0)+1=1$. Thus the origin is not an equilibrium of the unshifted system. The origin of the deviation coordinates represents $x=4$, the actual equilibrium. Studying stability around that point removes the affine constants and identifies the correct limiting state and command.
